12: ---
13: 
14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199: 
200: ---
201: 
202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
240: - Decision trees with multiple branches
241: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
242: - Systematic debugging procedures
243: 
244: **Technical Depth**:
245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes
249: 
250: **Size Threshold**:
251: - Content exceeds 200 lines
252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
254: 
255: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
256: 
257: **Core Content**:
258: - Overview and "When to Use"
259: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
260: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
261:   > **Note**: RULES sections in SKILL.md use ALL-CAPS H3 headers: `### ALWAYS`, `### NEVER`, `### ESCALATE IF` (or `####` at phase depth). See [skill-md-template.md](./skill-md-template.md) for the complete pattern.
262: - Quick reference
263: 
264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines
265: 
266: ### Reference File Types for AI Agent Skills
267: 
268: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
269: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |
270: | **Workflow**        | Multi-phase processes with checkpoints | `implementation-workflows.md` | 500-1500 lines |
271: | **Pattern Library** | Code patterns with before/after        | `shared-patterns.md`          | 300-800 lines  |
272: | **Standards**       | Rules and conventions                  | `code-quality-standards.md`   | 400-1000 lines |
273: | **Debugging**       | Systematic troubleshooting             | `debugging-workflows.md`      | 600-1200 lines |
274: | **Tool Guide**      | MCP/external tool integration          | `devtools-guide.md`           | 200-600 lines  |
275: | **Quick Reference** | Commands, shortcuts, checklists        | `quick-reference.md`          | 200-400 lines  |
276: 
277: **Note:** All authored reference file names use kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase).
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324: 
325: **Actions**:
326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
330: 
331: #### Phase 2: [Phase Name]
332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```
335: 
336: **Key Elements**:
337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
339: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead
340: 
341: ### Before/After Code Examples
342: 
343: **Purpose**: Show transformation from wrong to right
344: 
345: **Format**:
346: ```markdown
347: ### [Pattern Name]
348: 
349: **BEFORE**: [Problem description]
350: \```[language]
351: // Bad code with issues
352: // Showing what NOT to do
353: \```
354: 
355: **AFTER**: [Solution description]
356: \```[language]
357: // Good code with fixes
358: // Showing correct approach
359: \```
360: 
361: **Why better**: [Explanation of improvement]
362: ```
363: 
364: **Key Elements**:
365: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
366: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
367: - Inline comments explaining issues
368: - "Why better" rationale
369: 
370: ### Pattern Comparison Tables
371: 
372: **Purpose**: Compare approaches across scenarios
373: 
374: **Format**:
375: ```markdown
376: ### Common Patterns
377: 
378: | Scenario     | Approach A (Wrong) | Approach B (Right) | Why Better  |
379: | ------------ | ------------------ | ------------------ | ----------- |
380: | [Scenario 1] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
381: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
382: ```
383: 
384: **Use when**: Multiple scenarios need comparison
385: 
386: ### Decision Logic in Markdown
387: 
388: **Purpose**: Explicit if/then logic for workflow decisions
389: 
390: **Format**:
391: \```markdown
392: ### Decision Logic
393: 
394: \```markdown
395: IF [condition A]:
396:   → [Action/Path A]
397:   → [Expected outcome A]
398: 
399: IF [condition B]:
400:   → [Action/Path B]
401:   → [Expected outcome B]
402: 
403: IF [condition C]:
404:   → [Action/Path C]
405:   → [Expected outcome C]
406: \```
407: \```
408: 
409: **Alternative format** (decision tree):
410: \```markdown
411: \```
412: Analyze situation
413: ├─ Condition A met
414: │  └─ Execute Workflow A
415: │     └─ Expected outcome A
416: ├─ Condition B met
417: │  └─ Execute Workflow B
418: │     └─ Expected outcome B
419: └─ Condition C met
420:    └─ Execute Workflow C
421:       └─ Expected outcome C
422: \```
423: \```
424: 
425: ### Validation Checkpoints
426: 
427: **Purpose**: Named checkpoints throughout workflows
428: 
429: **Format**:
430: ```markdown
431: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
432: ```
433: 
434: **Examples**:
435: - `files_analyzed`
436: - `artifacts_filtered`
437: - `strategy_determined`
438: - `root_cause_identified`
439: 
440: **Usage**: Reference in quality checklists and debugging
441: 
442: ### Prerequisites Section
443: 
444: **Purpose**: Link to required standards and context
445: 
446: > **PLACEMENT**: Prerequisites go in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph.
447: 
448: **Format**:
449: ```markdown
450: # [Workflow Name]
451: 
452: [1-2 sentence summary only - no prerequisites here]
453: 
454: ---
455: 
456: \## 1. OVERVIEW
457: 
458: ### Prerequisites
459: Follow [standard name] for all implementations:
460: - **[Standard 1]**: [Brief description]
461: - **[Standard 2]**: [Brief description]
462: - See [standard-file.md](./standard-file.md) for complete requirements
463: ```
464: 
465: **Key Elements**:
466: - Appears in Section 1 OVERVIEW, not intro
467: - Links to other reference files
468: - Lists specific requirements
469: 
470: ### Tool Integration References
471: 
472: **Purpose**: Show MCP tool usage, script execution, asset references
473: 
474: **Format for MCP Tools**:
475: \```markdown
476: **Automated [Task] via MCP:**
477:

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle

94: ```

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.

206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale

209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting

213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:

857:     complex: [5, 10]

864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):

877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)

885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:

978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)

1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():

1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass

486:   phase_6_quality_check:
487:     action: "Review checklist + run AI quality evaluation"
488:     output: "Quality notes and improvement recommendations"
489:     depends_on: "phase_5_formatting"

492: ### YAML Configuration: Feature Flags

494: **Before (Markdown Table)**:

497: | ----------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------- |

524: ### YAML Workflow: Multi-Branch Decision Process
525: 
526: **Before (Markdown Prose)**:
527: ```markdown
528: The system should detect when to generate variants:
529: - If user explicitly requests options (shows me options, variations, different approaches)
530: - If complexity is high (7+) and uncertainty signals are present (not sure, what would work)
531: - Otherwise, generate single solution

539: **After (YAML Multi-Branch)**:

543:     explicit:
544:       keywords: ["show me options", "variations", "different approaches", "multiple designs"]
545:       action: "Generate variants immediately"
546:       priority: "high"
547: 
548:     implicit:

551:         - "uncertainty_signals present"

553:       action: "Generate variants with uncertainty disclaimer"
554:       priority: "medium"
555: 
556:     default:

558:       priority: "low"
559: 
560:   variant_count_guidelines:
561:     simple:
562:       complexity_range: [1, 3]
563:       variant_count: "2-3"
564: 
565:     standard:

567:       variant_count: "3-5"
568: 
569:     complex:
570:       complexity_range: [7, 10]

575:       override: true

675: ## 9. TEMPLATE GUIDELINES
676: 
677: ### Naming Conventions
678: 
679: **File Names** (kebab-case required):
680: - Format: `[topic]-[type].md`
681: - Use hyphens, not underscores
682: - Lowercase only
683: - Descriptive and specific
684: - Examples:
685:   - ✅ `frontmatter-templates.md`
686:   - ✅ `validation-reference.md`
687:   - ✅ `config-examples.yaml`
688:   - ✅ `packaging-guide.md`
689:   - ❌ `templates.md` (too generic)
690:   - ❌ `FrontmatterTemplates.md` (wrong case)
691:   - ❌ `frontmatter_templates.md` (underscores are not canonical)
692: 
693: **Type-Specific Patterns**:
694: 
695: | Asset Type | Naming Pattern           | Kebab-case Examples          |
696: | ---------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
697: | Template   | `[content]-templates.md` | `frontmatter-templates.md`   |
698: | Reference  | `[topic]-reference.md`   | `emoji-reference.md`         |
699: | Example    | `[topic]-examples.md`    | `optimization-examples.md`   |
700: | Guide      | `[process]-guide.md`     | `packaging-guide.md`         |
701: | Checklist  | `[topic]-checklist.md`   | `validation-checklist.md`    |
702: 
703: **Section Names**:
704: - Use title case
705: - Be descriptive but concise
706: - Number if sequential: `1. Template Name`
707: 
708: ### Content Organization
709: 
710: **Progressive Disclosure**:
711: 1. **Introduction**: What this is, why it exists (1-2 sentences)
712: 2. **Sections**: Each covers one topic completely
713: 3. **Examples**: Show, don't just tell
714: 4. **Quick Reference**: Summary at end (optional)
715: 
716: **Section Structure**:
717: - **Purpose**: Why this section exists
718: - **Guidelines**: How to use the content
719: - **Template**: Copy-paste starting point
720: - **Example**: Complete working example
721: 
722: ### Formatting Standards
723: 
724: **Code Blocks**:
725: - Always specify language: ` ```yaml `, ` ```markdown `, ` ```bash `
726: - Include comments explaining non-obvious parts
727: - Show complete, runnable examples
728: - Use placeholder values that are obviously placeholders
729: 
730: **Placeholders**:
731: - Format: `[descriptive-name]` or `your-value-here`
732: - Examples:
733:   - ✅ `[skill-name]`, `[feature-description]`, `your-project-name`
734:   - ❌ `xxx`, `placeholder`, `FIXME`
735: 
736: **Lists**:
737: - Use `-` for unordered lists
738: - Use `1.` for ordered lists
739: - Nested lists indent by 2 spaces
740: - Keep items parallel in structure
741: 
742: **Tables**:
743: - Include header row
744: - Align consistently (usually left-aligned)
745: - Keep rows concise (1-2 lines)
746: - Use for comparisons or reference data
747: 
748: ### Writing Style
749: 
750: **Clarity**:
751: - Write for someone unfamiliar with your skill
752: - Define domain-specific terms on first use
753: - Use active voice: "Create the file" not "The file should be created"
754: - Be concise but complete
755: 
756: **Examples**:
757: - Every template should have a complete example
758: - Show real-world usage, not toy examples
759: - Include common variations
760: - Annotate non-obvious parts
761: 
762: **Consistency**:
763: - Use same terminology throughout
764: - Follow patterns from other assets in the skill
765: - Match style of SKILL.md
766: - Use consistent formatting
767:

770: ## 10. ASSET FILE CHECKLIST
771: 
772: **Before creating an asset file, verify**:

799: ```

855: ## 12. ASSET MAINTENANCE
856: 
857: ### When to Update Assets
858: 
859: **Update asset files when**:
860: - New template variations emerge
861: - User feedback reveals confusion
862: - Standards or conventions change
863: - New use cases discovered
864: - Examples become outdated

866: **Version control**:

869: - Remove deprecated templates
870: - Add migration notes for breaking changes

872: ### Deprecation Strategy
873: 
874: **If removing a template**:
875: 1. Mark as deprecated in section header: `## DEPRECATED: Template Name`

14: # Skill Asset File Templates - Creation Guidelines
15: 
16: Templates and guidelines for creating asset files in AI agent skills.
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: ### Location & Naming
21: 
22: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/assets/`
23: 
24: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with the appropriate extension
25: 
26: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
27: |---------------|-----------------|
28: | `frontmatter-templates.md` | `FrontmatterTemplates.md` (PascalCase) |
29: | `config-examples.yaml` | `config_examples.yaml` (snake_case) |
30: | `validation-checklist.md` | `ValidationChecklist.MD` (wrong case) |
31: | `emoji-reference.md` | `emojiReference.md` (camelCase) |
32: 
33: ### When to Create Assets
34: 
35: **Create an asset file when:**
36: - Templates users apply repeatedly
37: - Reference data >50 lines and self-contained
38: - Multiple examples of same pattern exist
39: - Lookup tables or decision matrices needed
40: - Template variations for different scenarios
41: 
42: **Keep in SKILL.md when:**
43: - Content <30 lines
44: - Tightly coupled to workflow logic
45: - Needs to be visible immediately (not progressive disclosure)
46: - Part of core instructions (RULES, WORKFLOW sections)
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## 2. ASSET FILE TYPES
51: 
52: ### Template Files
53: **Purpose**: Provide copy-paste starting points for common tasks
54: 
55: **Naming**: `[content-type]-templates.md`
56: - Example: `frontmatter-templates.md`, `structure-templates.md`
57: 
58: **Structure**:
59: - One template per section
60: - Include field descriptions
61: - Show complete examples
62: - Explain when to use each template
63: 
64: **Use cases**:
65: - Document templates (SKILL.md, commands, knowledge files)
66: - Configuration templates (YAML, JSON)
67: - Code templates (functions, classes, modules)
68: 
69: ### Reference Files
70: **Purpose**: Provide lookup tables, decision trees, or reference data
71: 
72: **Naming**: `[topic]-reference.md`
73: - Example: `emoji-reference.md`, `validation-reference.md`
74: 
75: **Structure**:
76: - Tables or lists for quick lookup
77: - Decision matrices
78: - Classification systems
79: - Standards and conventions
80: 
81: **Use cases**:
82: - Emoji selection guides
83: - File type classifications
84: - Validation rule sets
85: - Naming conventions
86: 
87: ### Example Files
88: **Purpose**: Show working examples of skill outputs
89: 
90: **Naming**: `[topic]-examples.md`
91: - Example: `optimization-examples.md`, `skill-examples.md`
92: 
93: **Structure**:
94: - Before/after comparisons
95: - Annotated examples
96: - Multiple variations
97: - Anti-patterns to avoid
98: 
99: **Use cases**:
100: - Complete skill applications
101: - Common patterns
102: - Edge cases
103: - Quality standards
104: 
105: ### Guide Files
106: **Purpose**: Detailed how-to guides for complex processes
107: 
108: **Naming**: `[process]-guide.md`
109: - Example: `packaging-guide.md`, `distribution-guide.md`
110: 
111: **Structure**:
112: - Step-by-step instructions
113: - Troubleshooting sections
114: - Best practices
115: - Common pitfalls
116: 
117: **Use cases**:
118: - Multi-step processes
119: - Advanced techniques
120: - Workflow deep-dives
121: - Integration guides
122: 
123: ---
124: 
125: ## 3. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
126: 
127: ### Title and Intro
128: 
129: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
130: 
131: ```markdown
132: ---
133: title: [Title]
134: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
135: trigger_phrases:
136:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
137:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
138:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
139: importance_tier: normal
140: contextType: general
141: version: 1.0.0.0
142: ---
143: 
144: # [Title]
145: 
146: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
147: 
148: \## 1. OVERVIEW
149: 
150: ### Purpose
151: 
152: [Why this asset exists]
153: 
154: ### Usage
155: 
156: [How to use this asset - copy instructions, customization notes]
157: 
158: ---
159: 
160: \## 2. [Content Section]
161: 
162: [The actual template/checklist/snippet content]
163: 
164: ---
165: 
166: ## N. Related Resources (optional, if present must be last)
167: 
168: [Links to related files]
169: 
170: ```
171: 
172: Every asset file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content, `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, and `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
173: 
174: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and OVERVIEW section.**
175: > The intro is a hook. OVERVIEW provides the details.
176: 
177: #### GOOD Intro Structure
178: 
179: ```markdown
180: # Git Commit Templates
181: 
182: Copy the template that matches the change, fill the fields, and commit.
183: 
184: \## 1. OVERVIEW
185: 
186: ### Purpose
187: 
188: Uniform messages let a reader scan history by intent instead of by author.
189: 
190: ### Usage
191: 
192: Copy the appropriate template based on commit type...
193: 
194: ---
195: 
196: \## 2. COMMIT TEMPLATES
197: ...
198: ```
199: 
200: #### BAD Intro Structure (too long, has subsections)
201: 
202: ```markdown
203: # Git Commit Templates
204: 
205: Copy-paste templates for creating well-structured commit messages.
206: 
207: ### Core Principle    ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
208: Atomic commits with clear intent = maintainable history.
209: 
210: ### When to Use       ← WRONG: This belongs in OVERVIEW section!
211: - Creating new features
212: - Fixing bugs
213: 
214: ---
215: ```
216: 
217: ### Intro vs OVERVIEW Content Placement
218: 
219: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | OVERVIEW Section       |
220: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------- |
221: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat)    |
222: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Purpose)     |
223: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Purpose)     |
224: | How to copy/customize | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Usage)       |
225: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (in Usage)       |
226: | Any H2/H3 subsections | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES                  |
227: 
228: ---

16: 
17: This reference prevents a category error: Hermes profiles and `delegate_task` sub-agents are not persona surfaces for this repo's agents.

19: ## 1. OVERVIEW
20: 
21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: Records every route a repo persona can take into a Hermes dispatch, and the reason a profile or a `delegate_task` child cannot stand in for one.
24: 
25: ### When to Use
26: 
27: - Composing a dispatch that carries a resolved agent persona
28: - Deciding whether to preload `agent-<name>` or inline the persona
29: - Checking what a `delegate_task` child may and may not do
30: - Finding the prompt template for a nested `.skilled/commands` command
31: 
32: ### Core Principle
33: 
34: The repo's agents (`.skilled/agents/*.md`, the authored source) reach a Hermes dispatch only inside the prompt. Hermes has no flag that loads an agent file, its profiles are whole-home islands, and `delegate_task` children receive a goal and context, never an agent definition.
35:

38: ## 2. PERSONA ROUTES
39: 
40: | Route | Works | Use when |
41: |---|---|---|
42: | Inline the persona block at the top of the prompt, after the child-dispatch preamble | Yes | Default; the `cli-codex` and `cli-pi` precedent |
43: | Persona skill preloaded with `-s <name>` from `./.hermes/skills` | Yes, after the trust grant | Only if prompt size becomes a measured problem; needs the repo-local folder and the operator's trust |
44: | `hermes profile create` per agent | No | Profiles isolate homes and credentials, not personas |

15: # Hermes CLI Unique Capabilities
16: 
17: Reference for the Hermes surfaces that differ from `cli-codex`, `cli-claude-code`, `cli-opencode`, `cli-cursor`, `cli-devin` and `cli-pi`. Everything here is source-read on v0.21.1 unless marked observed; the contract pin records the live checks.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: Give a dispatcher the Hermes surfaces that behave unlike every sibling, so it knows what a leaf may rely on and what stays an operator step.
26: 
27: ### When to Use
28: 
29: - Choosing the `-t` toolset list for a leaf
30: - Checking whether a project skill or plugin will load
31: - Planning a write that lands inside `.hermes/`
32: - Deciding whether MCP, hooks or profiles can ship in the repo
33: 
34: ### Core Principle
35: 
36: Hermes exposes more of its surface through named toolsets and user-level configuration than any sibling, and it reads a repo's `.hermes/` folder for exactly two things: skills and plugins. Knowing which is which decides what a dispatch may rely on and what stays an operator step.
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 2. TOOLSETS
41: 
42: `-t LIST` replaces the configured toolset roster for the run. Toolsets relevant to dispatch (from `toolsets.py`):
43: 
44: | Toolset | Carries | Leaf policy |
45: |---|---|---|
46: | `terminal` | Shell execution | Included for write leaves |
47: | `file` | `read_file`, `write_file`, `patch`, `search_files` | Always: it is the only toolset that reads files. A read-only leaf keeps it without `terminal`, and the repo plugin refuses the write tools under `SPECKIT_HERMES_READ_ONLY=1` |
48: | `search` | `web_search` only (no file search) | Never as a stand-in for file reading; `web` covers it when web search is allowed |
49: | `skills` | Skill loading and management | Included for write leaves |
50: | `todo` | Task list | Always |
51: | `web` | `web_search`, `web_extract` | Per the web-search policy: `live` and `inherit` include it, `disabled` omits it |
52: | `<mcp server name>` | Every enabled tool of that server | Named explicitly (for example `code_mode`) or the server is invisible to the run (observed 2026-09-14) |
53: | `delegation` | `delegate_task` sub-agents | **Never** for a leaf: it spawns agents outside the runner's boundary |
54: | `memory` | Memory read and write | **Never** for a leaf: it bleeds state across sessions |
55: | `clarify` | Asks the user a question | **Never** headless: nobody answers |
56: | `browser`, `vision`, `code_execution`, `computer_use` | Heavier surfaces | Off unless the task names them |
57: 
58: Hermes's stock roster enables `delegation` and `memory`, which is why every dispatch passes an explicit list.
59: 
60: ---
61: 
62: ## 3. REPO-LOCAL SKILLS
63: 
64: Hermes loads project skills from `./.hermes/skills` and `./.agents/skills`, resolved from the nearest project root, but only after `hermes skills trust` has recorded the root in `skills.trusted_project_dirs` of the **user-level** config. The repo cannot carry the grant.
65: 
66: - Every project skill directory is **scanned in full at session start** by Hermes's static scanner, and a symlinked directory is walked like a real one: observed 2026-09-14, the whole-tree link ran the scanner for over ten minutes and quarantined every hub, and a single linked skill directory (`cli-hermes`) was quarantined on 37 findings from its references and scripts.
67: - The repo therefore ships `.hermes/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` as generated markdown-only copies of all 56 canonical `SKILL.md` files plus `agent-<name>` copies of the 12 shared agents (`sync-skills-hermes.cjs`), each naming its canonical source; a session starts in about 17 seconds and `-s <name>` preloads any of them (verified live for `sk-git`, `cli-hermes` and `system-spec-kit`).
68: - `hermes skills list` enumerates the loadable copies as `local` rows, 61 of the 68 on 2026-09-15; the earlier "no project rows" reading was an artifact of the symlink design, under which every skill was quarantined and therefore excluded from the index.
69: - All 174 files pass Hermes's hard validator (name, description, body, name matches directory). Every description exceeds the 60-character listing budget and is truncated with an ellipsis; loading is unaffected, routing signal is.
70: - Never use per-file symlinks either: the scanner flags a symlink resolving outside a skill directory as a critical traversal, and quarantine is per skill directory and fail-closed. Six of the copies (`cli-cursor`, `cli-devin`, `cli-opencode`, `deep-research`, `mcp-aside-devtools`, `sk-create-repo-rule`) are quarantined on prose patterns in their own text. A quarantine is total: the skill leaves the index, the listing and `skill_view`, and `-s <name>` fails with `Unknown skill(s): <name>` and exit 1 (observed 2026-09-15 on `cli-opencode`). Hermes has no configuration knob for it, so a quarantined skill reaches a dispatch only by having its text named in the prompt.
71: - `hermes skills list` reports the load result: a `local` row means the copy loaded, its absence means the scanner quarantined it. A live session with `-s <name>` quoting the skill remains the stronger proof, because the listing does not show what reached the model.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: ## 4. PROJECT PLUGINS
76: 
77: Native plugins load from `~/.hermes/plugins/<name>/` and, opt-in through `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS`, from `./.hermes/plugins/<name>/`, but only when the plugin's key is also listed under `plugins.enabled` in the user-level config; `hermes plugins enable` refuses a project key, so that line is added by hand (observed 2026-09-14). The plugin hook list covers `pre_tool_call`, `pre_verify`, `on_session_start`, `on_session_end`, `subagent_start`, `subagent_stop`, `pre_gateway_dispatch` and more (source-read: `hermes_cli/plugins.py`). This is the repo-carriable vehicle for the guard cores; see [hook-contract.md](./hook-contract.md).
78: 
79: ---
80: 
81: ## 5. THE `.hermes/` WRITE GUARD
82: 
83: Hermes's file tools treat any write whose immediate parent directory is `.hermes` as a protected-instruction write that requires approval (source-read: `tools/file_tools_write_guards.py`). A dispatched leaf therefore cannot author the repo's `.hermes/` files without `--yolo`, and those files are authored from outside Hermes.
84: 
85: ---
86: 
87: ## 6. PROFILES AND HOME
88: 
89: `--profile NAME` (or `-p`) sets `HERMES_HOME` before any module import, scoping config, `.env`, `auth.json`, sessions, memories, skills and logs to that home. Profiles are independent islands: a fresh one holds no credentials. The fan-out never sets a profile; shared home plus `--ignore-rules` is the posture until a seeded-credential contract exists.
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## 7. SUBSYSTEMS THAT STAY OFF
94: 
95: The curator, gateway, cron, kanban, voice and desktop subsystems are off by default and `chat` spawns none of them. `hermes pause` stops cron, kanban and gateway turns only, not a CLI dispatch. Telemetry is opt-in. Startup for `hermes --version` measured 0.86 seconds on this machine, a lower bound for a real dispatch.
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## 8. WHAT HERMES CANNOT CARRY IN THE REPO
100: 
101: Config (`config.yaml`), shell hooks and their consent allowlist, MCP servers (`mcp_servers:`), the provider block and the trust grant. Each is an operator step this skill documents; a dispatch never performs one.

18: This reference records the Hermes contract as read from the installed source (v0.21.1, upstream `dc90a75a`, git install at `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`) and from live help output on 2026-09-14. Claims marked **source-read** await the contract pin; the one live observation is marked **observed**.
19: 
20: Sources: [research synthesis](../../../../specs/cli-external-orchestration/071-cli-hermes-creation/001-deep-research/research/research.md), [contract pin](../../../../specs/cli-external-orchestration/071-cli-hermes-creation/002-hermes-contract-pin/implementation-summary.md).
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Be the single source a dispatcher checks before running Hermes, so every flag, exit code and approval rule a run depends on is looked up rather than remembered.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: - Composing or auditing a `hermes chat` dispatch command
31: - Looking up a flag, an exit code or an environment variable
32: - Deciding whether a run may write or must stay read-only
33: 
34: Hermes Agent is a Python agent CLI with a large tool surface (terminal, file, search, web, browser, vision, delegation, memory, skills, MCP) and a provider catalog of some forty providers. The binary is `hermes`; `hermes --version` prints the version, install method and install directory. Record the installed version at execution time.
35: 
36: Hermes has three headless forms, and only one is auditable:
37: 
38: | Form | Invocation | Stdout | Session id | Approvals |
39: |---|---|---|---|---|
40: | Quiet oneshot chat (**use this**) | `hermes chat -Q --oneshot -q "<prompt>"` or `--query-file <path>` | Final response only | `session_id: <id>` on stderr | Flagged actions blocked; `--yolo` lifts the gate |
41: | Non-TTY chat | `hermes chat -q "<prompt>"` with stdio not a TTY | Response plus banner and previews unless `-Q` | On stderr | Same as above |
42: | Top-level oneshot (**never for dispatch**) | `hermes -z "<prompt>"` | Final response only | None | Auto-approves everything and auto-accepts hooks |
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 2. FLAGS THAT MATTER FOR DISPATCH
47: 
48: | Flag | Effect | Standing |
49: |---|---|---|
50: | `-q, --query TEXT` | The prompt in argv; on a non-TTY it answers and exits | live help |
51: | `--query-file PATH` | Read the prompt from a file, `-` for stdin, nothing shell-interpreted; mutually exclusive with `-q` | live help |
52: | `--oneshot` | Answer and exit; implied on non-TTY stdio and by `-Q` | live help |
53: | `-Q, --quiet` | Suppress banner, spinner and tool previews; print only the final response and session info | live help |
54: | `-m, --model ID` | Model id for this run | live help |
55: | `--provider NAME` | Built-in provider or a user-defined name from `providers:` in `config.yaml`; the packet pins `llmgateway` | live help |
56: | `--reasoning LEVEL` | `none minimal low medium high xhigh max ultra`, the same set as the runtime's effort enum | live help |
57: | `-t, --toolsets LIST` | Comma-separated toolsets to enable; replaces the configured set | live help |
58: | `-s, --skills LIST` | Preload skills for the session | live help |
59: | `--yolo` | Auto-approve the tool calls Hermes flags as dangerous; ordinary writes need no flag (observed 2026-09-14) | live help |
60: | `--ignore-rules` | Skip `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `.cursorrules` and memory injection. Hermes's help text also claims it skips preloaded skills; a live A/B disproved that, so `-s` and this flag travel together | live help, preload clause **corrected by observation 2026-09-15** |
61: | `--ignore-user-config` | Ignore `~/.hermes/config.yaml`; `.env` credentials still load | live help |
62: | `--safe-mode` | Disable user config, rules, plugins and MCP servers | live help |
63: | `--max-turns N` | Turn cap for the run (Hermes default 500) | live help |
64: | `--run-budget SECONDS` | Wall-clock budget; the agent wraps up as it expires | live help |
65: | `--source tool` | Keep the run out of the operator's session lists | live help |
66: | `--in DIR` | Change into DIR before starting | live help |
67: | `--accept-hooks` | Auto-approve unseen shell hooks; never pass unless the operator declared hooks | live help |
68: | `--worktree` | Run in an isolated git worktree; **never pass from a dispatch** (writes `.git/worktrees/` inside the repo) | live help |
69: | `--pass-session-id` | Put the session id into the system prompt | live help |
70: | `--resume ID`, `-c NAME` | Resume a session; not used by dispatch | live help |
71: 
72: ---
73: 
74: ## 3. EXIT CODES AND OUTPUT
75: 
76: | Case | Exit | Where the signal is | Standing |
77: |---|---|---|---|
78: | Completed turn with a response | 0 | Response on stdout, `session_id:` on stderr; with `deepseek-v4.1-flash` the model's reasoning precedes the answer on stdout | **observed 2026-09-14** (smoke: `OK` in 19 s) |
79: | Turn ended without a response | 0 with **empty stdout** | Seen when a deferred-tool loop ended the turn (`'read_file' is not a deferrable tool` on a toolset without `file`); exit 0 is not proof of an answer, so a caller requires non-empty stdout | **observed 2026-09-14** |
80: | `result.failed` | 1 | The gateway error on stdout (`HTTP 400: Requested model ... not supported`), `session_id:` still on stderr | **observed 2026-09-14** |
81: | Interrupt | 130 | | source-read |
82: | No provider configured | 1 | `No inference provider configured. Run 'hermes model' ...` on **stdout**; stderr empty; no `session_id:` | **observed 2026-09-14** |
83: | Run-budget expiry | 0 with a partial response | No distinct code or marker; `--run-budget 15` ended at 40 s. A silent provider stream is not bounded by the budget: the stale-stream watchdog fires at 600 s and retries | **observed 2026-09-14** |
84: | Top-level `-z` usage error | 2 | | source-read (`hermes_cli/oneshot.py`) |
85: 
86: The process ends in a hard exit after flushing, so a late handler cannot flip the code. Read the exit code first, then stdout for the response or the pre-flight message, then stderr for `session_id:` and `Error:`.
87: 
88: ---
89: 
90: ## 4. APPROVALS AND WRITES
91: 
92: Observed 2026-09-14, correcting the source-read claim the research carried:
93: 
94: - **Ordinary writes and commands need no flag.** A headless `chat -q` runs them without approval.
95: - **Only a flagged call reaches the approval gate.** That covers Hermes's dangerous-command pattern set, for example `rm -rf <path>`, and a write whose immediate parent directory is `.hermes`.
96: - **A blocked call says so.** In single-query mode without `--yolo` the call is blocked with `BLOCKED: Command flagged as dangerous (...) but single-query mode (-q) runs without a user present to approve it`.
97: - **`--yolo` lifts that gate.** `approvals.single_query_mode: approve` in `config.yaml` does the same globally. Hardline floors stay blocked even under `--yolo`.
98: - **There is no OS sandbox flag.** A read-only dispatch is read-only because its `-t` list omits `terminal` and `file`.
99: - **Terminal backends** (docker, ssh, modal and others) are config-level hardening, not per-run flags.
100: 
101: ---
102: 
103: ## 5. ISOLATION
104: 
105: - `--ignore-rules` removes `SOUL.md`, memories, session search and the CWD instruction files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`) from the prompt. Every dispatch passes it.
106: - `--safe-mode` additionally disables plugins and MCP servers; use it when a configured MCP server would add cold-start latency the dispatch does not need.
107: - `HERMES_HOME` (or `--profile`) relocates the whole home, including `.env` and `auth.json`. A fresh home is logged out of every provider, so the fan-out never sets it; per-lineage profiles wait for a seeded-credential contract.
108: - Writes to sessions, memories, logs and checkpoints land under `~/.hermes`, outside the repository and invisible to the fan-out containment guard.
109: 
110: ---
111: 
112: ## 6. ENVIRONMENT
113: 
114: | Variable | Set by | Meaning |
115: |---|---|---|
116: | `HERMES_AGENT=true` | Hermes, on every process | Self-invocation marker inherited by child processes (source-read: `hermes_cli/main.py`) |
117: | `HERMES_SESSION_ID` | Hermes, at agent init | Session marker inherited by children; the runtime's session env for this kind |
118: | `HERMES_HOME` | Operator or `--profile` | Home override; detection only for the runtime |
119: | `HERMES_YOLO_MODE=1`, `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1` | `hermes -z` | Auto-set by the top-level oneshot; one reason it is never used |
120: | `HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS` | Operator | Opt-in for `./.hermes/plugins/` |
121: | `LLMGATEWAY_API_KEY` | Operator, in `~/.hermes/.env` or the shell | The `key_env` the `llmgateway` provider block names |
122: | `SPECKIT_HERMES_STATE_DIR` | The fan-out runner | Per-lineage detection hint, never a home relocation |
123: | `SPECKIT_HERMES_READ_ONLY` | The fan-out runner, on a read-only lineage | The repo plugin refuses `write_file`, `patch`, `terminal`, `process_manage` and `execute_code` |
124: | `HERMES_SPEC_FOLDER` | The fan-out runner, or a caller | Repo-relative packet path. The repo plugin binds that packet to the session through the shared goal core and renders its goal brief into the session prompt |
125: | `HERMES_AGENT_PERSONA` | A caller | Agent name; the repo plugin binds it as the session persona and points at the preloaded skill `agent-<name>` (pass `-s agent-<name>`; a prompt section is capped at 4000 characters, so the full persona travels as the skill) |
126: 
127: Hermes loads `~/.hermes/.env` itself, so a key kept there needs no pass-through from the dispatching shell.
128: 
129: ---
130: 
131: ## 7. THE SAFE DISPATCH SHAPE
132: 
133: ```bash
134: hermes chat -Q --oneshot --query-file <prompt.md> --provider llmgateway --model <roster-id> \
135:   --reasoning max --ignore-rules --source tool --max-turns 200 --run-budget <timeout-60> \
136:   -t terminal,file,skills,todo,web [--yolo] --in <repo-root> </dev/null
137: ```
138: 
139: Read-only: omit `--yolo`, use `-t file,todo` (Hermes's `search` toolset is web search only; `read_file` and `search_files` live in `file` with the write tools) and set `SPECKIT_HERMES_READ_ONLY=1` so the repo plugin refuses `write_file` and `patch`. The fan-out builder emits this shape with `--query-file -` and the prompt on stdin, and without `--in` because the runner spawns in the repo root.
140: 
141: ---
142: 
143: ## 8. MANAGEMENT COMMANDS A DISPATCH NEVER RUNS
144: 
145: Never run:
146: 
147: - `hermes skills trust|install|update`
148: - `hermes mcp add|remove`
149: - `hermes plugins install|enable`
150: - `hermes config set`
151: - `hermes import-agent`
152: - `hermes setup`, `hermes update`
153: - `hermes profile create|use`
154: 
155: Each changes the operator's `~/.hermes`. A prompt that needs one stops and reports.
156: 
157: Read-only commands a dispatch may run, always with stdin closed:
158: 
159: - `hermes --version`
160: - `hermes status` (which does not show custom providers)
161: - `hermes doctor`
162: - `hermes config show|get`
163: - `hermes tools list`, `hermes skills list`, `hermes plugins list`, `hermes mcp list`, `hermes hooks list`
164: - `hermes prompt-size`

18: Orchestrate Hermes Agent (Nous Research's open-source, Python-based agent CLI) for quiet oneshot
19: coding dispatch, cross-AI validation, and model routing through the operator's LLM Gateway
20: provider. The evidence base is the research synthesis and the contract pin:
21: [research synthesis](../../../specs/cli-external-orchestration/071-cli-hermes-creation/001-deep-research/research/research.md),

24: unconfirmed until a live run records otherwise.
25:

27: deep-loop runtime, validate the returned output, and keep the calling AI as conductor.

31: ## 1. WHEN TO USE
32: 
33: ### Activation Triggers
34:

75: Do not add a packet-local wrapper, spawn path, or command builder.

81: - The `-1017` id is the rotation default.
82: - These are bare literals of Pi's roster, and every one was probed live.
83: - GPT-6 Luna and GPT-6 Sol are off this roster. GPT models run only on the GPT provider, through cli-codex or Pi's `openai` route.

88: 
89: ~~~bash
90: hermes chat -Q --oneshot --query-file <prompt.md> --provider llmgateway --model deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
91:   --reasoning max --ignore-rules --source tool --max-turns 200 --run-budget 840 \
92:   -t terminal,file,skills,todo,web --yolo --in <repo-root> </dev/null
93: ~~~
94: 
95: - `chat -Q --oneshot` is the auditable headless form: response on stdout, `session_id: <id>` on stderr, hard exit codes (0 success, 1 `result.failed`, 130 interrupt). Never `hermes -z`: it drops the session id and auto-approves everything.
96: - `--query-file` reads the prompt verbatim; `-` reads stdin, which is how the fan-out builder passes it. Argv `-q` is for short prompts only.
97: - `--yolo` is required for writes; a read-only dispatch omits it and narrows `-t` to `file,todo`.
98: - `--run-budget` stays one margin under the caller's timeout because budget expiry has no distinct exit code; the in-agent wrap-up must win the race.
99: - `--in <repo-root>` pins the working directory on a manual dispatch; the fan-out omits it because the runner already spawns in the repo root.

102:

104: 2. Classify the request as write, read-only review, or generation; pick the toolset accordingly.
105: 3. Compose the prompt using [prompt-quality-card.md](./assets/prompt-quality-card.md), persona inlined.
106: 4. Pass a research or review lineage to the shared deep-loop runtime; run a single build or doc dispatch with the dispatch shape above.
107: 5. Capture stdout (the response) and stderr (`session_id:`, `Error:`) separately.
108: 6. Validate the output, changed files, and required tests before handback.

112: - **No provider configured means exit 1 with the reason on stdout, not stderr.** Observed live 2026-09-14 before the provider block existed: `No inference provider configured. Run 'hermes model' ...` printed to stdout, stderr empty, no `session_id:` line. Read the exit code, then stdout.
113: - **`--yolo` lifts only the dangerous-action gate.** Observed live 2026-09-14:
114:   - Without `--yolo`, a headless chat wrote an ordinary scratch file (exit 0).
115:   - `rm -rf <scratch dir>` came back `BLOCKED: Command flagged as dangerous ... single-query mode (-q) runs without a user present to approve it`.
116:   - With `--yolo`, the same command ran.
117: - Ordinary writes and commands need no flag. A read-only dispatch is read-only because of its `-t` list, not because `--yolo` is absent.
118: - **`--ignore-rules` is not optional.** Hermes injects `SOUL.md`, memories, session search, and the CWD `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `.cursorrules` unless told not to.
119: - **`--worktree` writes inside the repo.** It runs `git worktree add`, which the fan-out containment guard reverts as an out-of-lineage write.

123: - **Project skills load only after `hermes skills trust`.** The repo mirrors every skill as a generated markdown-only copy under `.hermes/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (`sync-skills-hermes.cjs`), never as a symlink.

125: - Preload with `-s <name>`. `hermes skills list` shows the loadable copies as `local` rows, and a copy the scanner quarantines is absent from both the listing and `-s`.
126: - See [hermes-tools.md](./references/hermes-tools.md).
127: - **`-Q` stdout can carry the model's reasoning before the answer** (observed with `deepseek-v4.1-flash` through the gateway). Read the tail for the answer; the fan-out validates artifacts, not stdout.

129: - **`--run-budget` does not bound a stalled provider stream.** Hermes's stale-stream watchdog fires at 600 seconds and retries; the caller's own timeout is the real bound.
130: - **MCP servers are reached only when named in `-t`.** `-t file,todo` hides a configured server; `-t file,todo,code_mode` reaches it.

135: 
136: ### ✅ ALWAYS
137:

140: 3. Use `chat -Q --oneshot` with `--query-file`; pass `--yolo` for writes and omit it for read-only work.
141: 4. Pass `--ignore-rules`, `--source tool`, and an explicit `-t` list without `delegation` and `memory`.
142: 5. Keep `--run-budget` under the caller's timeout and read the exit code, then stdout and stderr.
143: 6. Use the prompt-quality card's two-tier precedence rule.
144: 7. Validate Hermes-generated changes with the repository's code and test gates.
145: 8. Keep the current runtime as conductor and Hermes as delegated executor.
146: 9. Treat source-read claims as confirmed only when the contract pin records the live run.
147: 10. Compose every dispatch as `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}`, never a bare task.
148:     - Resolve the persona from the CALLING runtime's agent directory (AGENTS.md §9), and INLINE it in the prompt.
149:     - No native persona surface exists: Hermes carries no agent directory of its own, and Hermes profiles are whole-home islands, so `delegate_task` children cannot read agent files.
150:     - Canonical contract: `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection".

152: 
153: ### ⛔ NEVER
154: 
155: 1. Never dispatch when `command -v hermes` fails.
156: 2. Never dispatch Hermes from inside Hermes, from inside a fan-out lineage, or when `cli-hermes` already appears in the dispatch stack.
157: 3. Never build a second Hermes adapter inside this packet.
158: 4. Never use `hermes -z` for an auditable dispatch, and never pass `--worktree`.
159: 5. Never run `hermes import-agent`: it copies repo state into the user home and bypasses the trust and quarantine path.
160: 6. Never claim a repo file configures Hermes hooks, MCP servers, or the provider; those are operator steps.
161: 7. Never pass an off-roster model id or a provider-prefixed id.
162: 8. Never pass secrets or provider keys in prompts.
163: 
164: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
165: 
166: 1. Hermes is missing from PATH or `hermes config get providers.llmgateway.base_url` prints nothing.
167: 2. The task needs a model outside the closed roster.
168: 3. The task depends on a source-read behavior the contract pin has not yet confirmed.
169: 4. The task requests `hermes skills trust`, `hermes mcp add`, or a config change; those are the operator's.
170: 5. A Hermes plugin or hook would need `--accept-hooks`.

173: 
174: ## 5. REFERENCES
